messages:
devon: Heads-up: during the EU->US preemptible reclaim last night the us-west gpupool spun up ~20 replacement nodes and ~6 are stuck NotReady/NoSchedule.
infra-bot: Alert: gpu-nodepool-uswest scaled to 20 at 2024-11-02T03:00Z -> 6 nodes NotReady (device-plugin failure).
maria: grabbing journal from one of the affected nodes, cutting the noise: 
```
Nov 02 03:12:07 kubelet[1234]: E1102 03:12:07.123456  1234 device_plugin.go:212] failed to start device plugin: listen unix /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/nvidia.sock: bind: address already in use
Nov 02 03:12:07 kubelet[1234]: E1102 03:12:07.123789  1234 device_plugin.go:230] registration failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: connection is closing"
Nov 02 03:12:07 kernel: udev: change event flood (nvlink?), 400 events/sec
```
devon: interesting — not the usual kernel module crash. socket already in use + udev flood smells like leftover sockets from previous instance + thundering-herd startup.
sam: cluster-autoscaler also shows repeated scale-ups then deletes because new nodes never Ready: 
```
I1102 03:13:10 cluster_autoscaler.go:921] Scale-up: Launching 4 nodes in "us-west" (node group gpu-nodepool-uswest). Reason: pending pods: 120
I1102 03:15:40 cluster_autoscaler.go:1045] Scale-down: Removing empty node "gpunode-zzzz" (not ready for 150s)
```
maria: bonus cost impact: since they were preemptible the autoscaler retried 3x over 45 minutes -> ~6 extra instance-hours billed. finance pinged. :grimacing: 
oncall: From oncall: root cause likely twofold — (1) device-plugin restart concurrency hitting the same unix socket path causing EADDRINUSE, (2) udev/device hotplug flood blocking kubelet device plugin registration window.
devon: quick mitigation applied: rolled the nvidia-device-plugin DaemonSet to add `initContainer` that waits random 0-20s before starting plugin so they don't all race for socket. also added `livenessProbe` backoff to avoid tight crash loops.
maria: confirming logs after the roll: one node had `bind: address already in use` for 3 restarts, then cleaned up and succeeded after init delay. udev flood reduced after bumping kernel udev rate limit via sysctl on the node image.
sam: long term: propose two changes: (1) stagger node creation in the autoscaler cloudprovider: enable nodegroup launch jitter so we don't get 20 launches at once for one AZ; (2) change device-plugin to use per-node unique socket path (or ensure old socket removed on startup).
devon: filed infra ticket INFRA-1247 with suggested fixes and rollout plan. Also opened PR to daemonset to set `--socket-dir=/var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/nvidia-$(NODE_NAME)` env for safety.
maria: note for ops playbook: if you see a cluster-autoscaler loop + >3 NotReady GPUs in a row: 1) don't scale down the pool immediately, 2) rollout device-plugin with init sleep, 3) check /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins for leftover sockets and rm -f, 4) if udev event flood, throttle via `udevadm control --stop-exec-queue` or lift udev_rate_limit in image.
oncall: marking incident resolved for now, reopening if any node remains NotReady after 30m. :white_check_mark:
sam: FYI, I also added a short Grafana alert rule: gpupool.register_fail_rate > 5% for 10m -> page oncall.
